To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cross section of the N N --> n n pi pi reaction is dominated by the N* excitation mechanism.

the N N --> p N pi pi, N N --> N p pi pi, and N N --> N (p n) pi pi reactions have cross sections that increase with energy, and that the pion angular distributions are peaked in the backward hemisphere, in agreement with data.
the N N --> n n pi+ pi+ reaction is dominated by the excitation of the N*(1440) resonance and the N N --> p p pi- pi- reaction is dominated by Delta excitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the two pion production mechanism in N-N collisions at intermediate energies.
two main aspects: 1) the study of the production of two pions in nucleon-nucleon collisions at intermediate energies, and 2) the study of two pion production in nucleon-nuclear reactions.
the study of two pion production in nucleon-nucleon collisions, at energies ranging from the pion production threshold to 1 GeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N* excitation mechanism is dominant for the T=0 channels, while the Delta excitation mechanism is important for the T=1 channels.

the N N --> p p pi+ pi- reaction is a very interesting reaction for a variety of reasons: it can be measured in the laboratory and the results are not obscured by background reactions, the reaction mechanism is very well understood in the region where pions are produced in an isospinning zero state, the cross sections are very large, the reaction is a good source of information on the pion pion interaction and the reaction is a very sensitive probe of the nucleon nucleon interaction.
the reaction mechanism for the N N--> N N (pi pi) is not yet understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N* mechanism is dominant at low energies and that the Delta mechanism is dominant at high energies.
we have developed a consistent model for N N --> N pi pi reactions at intermediate energies and that it can be used for the analysis of experimental data.
the N* excitation is the dominant mechanism in all channels at low energies and that the Delta excitation is the most important at higher energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N* mechanism is dominant at energies below 500 MeV and that it can be described in terms of a simple model, with a single free parameter.
the isoscalar source, which has been shown in other work to be important for the N N pi pi channels at lower energies, is also important at higher energies and for the charged channels.
there is a large cross section for N N --> N pi pi at energies of a few GeV.
